title: Interactive console journey templates: guided onboarding, empty states, and contextual micro-tours
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and prototype a set of reusable interactive journey templates for the Redwood Console that cover first-time onboarding (account -> API key -> first request), empty states for Dashboards / Rollouts / Cost views, and in-product micro-tours/tooltips tied to user goals. Templates should be componentized for productization (copy + step config + analytics hooks) and include accessibility considerations and localization placeholders.
motivation: New and infrequent Console users struggle to complete the critical path of creating an API key, running a first request, and seeing cost impact. Empty states across dashboards and rollouts are inconsistent and miss conversion moments. Providing guided, reusable journeys will reduce time-to-first-success, lower support asks, and increase feature adoption.
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity Figma screens for three journey templates: onboarding-first-request, dashboards-empty, rollouts-empty
Interactive clickable prototype (Figma + Framer-lite) that covers optimistic/edge flows
Design tokens and copy variants exported as a single doc for engineering (component props and analytics hook names)
Accessibility checklist completed (keyboard flow, focus rings, screen-reader hints) and contrast checks
Design review signed off by PM and Eng lead and a dev-handoff meeting scheduled
tasks: Map critical user paths and success metrics (time-to-first-request, completion rate)
Draft microcopy variations for CTAs, onboarding steps, and empty-state prompts
Create modular components: coachmark, stepper modal, contextual tooltip, template config schema example
Prototype happy path + two failure paths (API key creation blocked, quota limit)
Run 5 moderated usability tests with new users and iterate on wording and reveal timing
Compile dev-handoff artifact and record 30-min walkthrough
notes: Initial concept workshop ran 2026-02-12: consensus to prioritize onboarding -> dashboards -> rollouts in that order.
Decision: use dismissible coachmarks instead of full-screen tours to avoid blocking customers during critical tasks.
Trade-off: persistent checklist sidebar was deprioritized due to engineering cost; will prototype later if metrics justify.
Localization: keep copy tokens generic; provide 2-line and 3-line fallbacks for translations.
Analytics: suggested events: onboarding.started, onboarding.step_completed, empty_state.cta_clicked, tour.dismissed
review_feedback: PM Jonas: prefer a single CTA for first-request flow that creates API key + example request to reduce cognitive load.
Eng Priya: ensure templates expose a lightweight config API (startStep, disabledSteps, analyticsNamespace).
Accessibility review (Anika): add aria-live updates for each step and ensure focus trap is temporary for tooltips.
Growth Linh: propose an A/B test comparing coachmark vs inline banner for dashboards-empty to measure activation lift.
usability_plan: Recruit 5 participants unfamiliar with Redwood Console (non-technical product managers / devs)
Tasks: sign up -> create API key -> run a sample request -> open Dashboard -> respond to empty-state CTA
Metrics: success rate, time-on-task, number of hints needed, SUS subjective score
handoff_artifacts: Figma file with component variants and tokens
Spec doc (Confluence) with JSON example of template config and analytics events
Prototype link and 10-min demo recording (uploaded to drive)
next_steps: Address review feedback from Eng and Accessibility by 2026-03-14
Run moderated usability sessions and capture heatmaps
Prepare a 20-minute demo for the March 18 all-hands product sync
Create a lightweight implementation spike ticket for ENG-2431
